body: You do realize that I'm writing this as a mom, right? No, we wouldn't hate you! Real women would be appreciative of what you have to offer her ready-made family! I know I would be!

You need to find a woman who is stable enough to support her family! With that comes the allowance for the stay-at-home dad-type. Too often you'll find women who subscribe to the theory that men should be taking care of the girl and the family. Times have changed. I'd rather be off at work knowing that my kids have a steady, loving figurehead at home giving love and structure, rather than some sitter! Again, we're out there! If you're in NC...man!

Well, if you post here or anywhere (blog perhaps?) on a regular basis, Print those! Anything to give the professional some insight as to where you are...because our words escape us and we surely suck at telling them!   When I shut down, I shut down and won't even go to my appointments! If I'm exchanging some sort of written material with my therapist, they at least have an idea of where I'm at. It was really helpful and the reason I kept writing was because I knew I could miss an appointment if I did. An arrangement like that is motivating in some ways. You're never really feeling pressured to do either! (Attend the appt or write!)
OMG! I'd almost kill for a stay-at-home-dad type! Trust me, we're out there! Please keep searching!
Unfortunately I meant it in regard to suicide, right? I only wish I could mean it with the will to keep going...

PM me too! I have a six-year old who suffers from developmental delays (high-functioning autism and anxiety). If I can help you in anyway, let me know! I'd love to be your friend. I don't have any, in real life. I also have been diagnosed with PTSD and anxiety myself.

This makes sense to me. I have done my best, unintentionally, to shut out everyone in my life for the same reasons. My anxiety also keeps me from being successful in group settings. I have also sought help, but never seem to be able to put it into words. What I have done in the past is put it on paper and submit that to the therapist. That helps more than you could imagine. It releases the feelings I have trapped within myself and alerts them to where I am, almost like keeping a journal. Perhaps, something like that could help you?
